scenes.tts: Cohen injected newborn mice every day with a crude extract of male mouse salivary gland. A crude extract is a mixture, not a single purified protein. He expected a particular result. The sympathetic ganglia should be enlarged. And they were.
scenes.visual: A mouse pup in simple shapes. A syringe injects, a vial of crude extract is named a mixture. Small ganglia blobs inside the pup get a dashed expected outline, then grow to fill it.
scenes.narration: Cohen injected newborn mice every day with a crude extract of male mouse salivary gland. A crude extract is a mixture, not a single purified protein. He expected a particular result. The sympathetic ganglia should be enlarged. And they were.

scenes.tts: But the mice did something else as well. They opened their eyelids about seven days after birth. The usual age is twelve to fourteen days. Their teeth also came through early. That did not fit. Neither of these was expected.
scenes.visual: The same pup with enlarged ganglia. A question mark, then the closed eye opens as a marker lands at about 7 on a days-after-birth line, with a grey band at 12 to 14. Teeth appear on the pup. Both new effects are tagged as not expected.
scenes.narration: But the mice did something else as well. They opened their eyelids about seven days after birth. The usual age is twelve to fourteen days. Their teeth also came through early. That did not fit. Neither of these was expected.

scenes.tts: Purified nerve growth factor, given alone, did none of that. So the crude extract must have carried a second protein, with its own activity. This one acts on skin, so it was named epidermal growth factor. One extract, two proteins, two activities.
scenes.visual: Top row: purified nerve growth factor leads to eyelids early and teeth early, both struck out. Below, the crude extract splits into nerve growth factor and a second protein, each pointing to its own effect. The second protein is labelled acts on skin and renamed epidermal growth factor.
scenes.narration: Purified nerve growth factor, given alone, did none of that. So the crude extract must have carried a second protein, with its own activity. This one acts on skin, so it was named epidermal growth factor. One extract, two proteins, two activities.

scenes.tts: The halo assay counted nerve fibers, and only nerve fibers. It could not show eyelids or teeth, so it was blind to epidermal growth factor. A whole newborn mouse responds to everything in a crude extract. When you start from a mixture, the assay you choose decides which molecule you find.
scenes.visual: Left: a ganglion with a halo of fibers, labelled halo assay, counts nerve fibers. Epidermal growth factor sits beside it and nothing happens: blind. Right: the whole mouse with all three effects. A closing line says the assay decides which molecule you find.
